title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G = GL(2) and SG = SL(2), probably over a base like Z or Q. T_0 is the centre G_m of G. T_rho and T_sigma are tori in G attached to two elements rho and sigma; these are plausibly the elliptic elements of order 3 (or 6) and order 4 in PSL2(Z)/SL2(Z), the 'rho' and 'sigma' of the loop equations. N'_sigma is a normaliser-type group. G*_{rho,sigma}(0) is a group scheme defined on an earlier manuscript page (p. 487'(20)) and sits inside T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma. The group scheme M_{rho,sigma} is defined as the product G*_{rho,sigma}(0).SG. Its neutral component M^0 embeds in T_rho x T_sigma x G as the triples (x,y,f) with det x = det y = det f (previous page, (16)).

The theorem on this page records the following structure.
(20) M is an extension 1 -> M^0 -> M -> mu2 x mu2 -> 1. The map to mu2 x mu2 comes from G* -> mu2 x mu2, written roughly (alpha,beta,mu,eps) -> (det alpha, eps det b).
(21) ST_rho x ST_sigma, the norm-one subtori, is a central subgroup of M.
(22) There is an exact sequence 1 -> ST_rho x ST_sigma -> M^0 --Theta--> G -> 1, where Theta is projection to the third factor, and SG embeds in M^0.
(NB) J^0 = Ker(M^0 -> PG), which is isomorphic to T_rho x_{G_m} T_sigma, is central in M.
(23) There is an exact sequence 1 -> ST_rho x ST_sigma x SG -> M -> G_m x mu2 x mu2 -> 1. Equivalently, (24): M^{0+} := Ker(chi = det : M^0 -> G_m) is isomorphic to ST_rho x ST_sigma x SG.
(25) The centres mu2 of ST_rho, ST_sigma and SG give a canonical embedding mu2^3 -> M^{0+}. The next page turns this into canonical 'liens' Sigma = (Z/2)^3 -> Gamma M^{0+}.

Purpose. Grothendieck is building algebraic group-scheme analogues of the Teichmüller-type groups M_{0,3}, \hat{G}^+_{0,3} and T^!_{0,3}. These are linear-algebraic 'paraphrases' of the profinite or discrete objects that enter the loop equations (equations des lacets) of the Galois-Teichmüller tower. The next page sets G^+_{rho,sigma} = SG ~ SL2 and introduces a quotient T_{rho,sigma} together with a semidirect splitting.

Verification. (22) and (24) follow directly from the description in (16). The kernel of the projection to G is {(x,y,1) : det x = det y = 1}. The kernel of det is ST_rho x ST_sigma x SG.
errors: (23) writes the quotient M/M^{0+} as the direct product G_m x mu2 x mu2. A priori it is only an extension of mu2 x mu2 by G_m, and the page gives no argument that it is commutative and split.
The NB line 'J^0 ∩ SG ≃ ...' is left incomplete. From (17), J^0 meets SG in the scalars ±1, i.e. mu2; this is not stated explicitly.

The isomorphism symbol in (19) is labelled 'déf', so it is a definition rather than an isomorphism. The inclusion of G*(0) in T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma depends on the earlier page and cannot be checked here.

ideas.what: Algebraic group-scheme model M_{rho,sigma}, built from GL2/SL2 and the tori attached to the elliptic elements rho and sigma, imitating the Teichmüller groups M_{0,3} and T_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Linear-algebraic / motivic analogues of Galois-Teichmüller groups; Zariski closures of Teichmüller modular groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related ideas: Ihara, Drinfeld (GRT), Deligne, Hain–Matsumoto (relative completion of mapping class groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower but not these GL2 group schemes

ideas.what: Dévissage of M via exact sequences with central torus kernel ST_rho x ST_sigma and quotient GL2, plus the identification M^{0+} ≅ ST_rho x ST_sigma x SL2
ideas.modern_name: Extension structure of an algebraic group (central extensions, component group)

ideas.what: Canonical embedding of (Z/2)^3, the centres of the three norm-one factors, giving 'liens'

missed.claim: This page is part of a systematic attempt to replace the profinite Teichmüller-tower objects (M_{0,3}, T^!_{0,3}, \hat{G}^+_{0,3}) by algebraic group schemes over GL2/SL2 with tori attached to the elliptic points rho and sigma. The aim is apparently to 'paraphrase' the loop equations in an algebraic-group setting. The construction does not appear in the literature in this form, but on this page it consists of routine structural bookkeeping.
missed.quote: Je vais introduire au sujet des groupes M_{ρ,σ} des notations qui paraphrasent les notations M_{0,3} etc, dans le contexte des schémas en groupes (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is loosely related to relative/Malcev completions of SL2(Z) (Hain) and to the motivic Galois–Teichmüller programme. It may be of interest for reconstructing the intent of Grothendieck's algebraic models; the page itself has no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The structural exact sequences are elementary consequences of the definitions. The only notable aspect is the unpublished programme of algebraic-group models of Teichmüller-tower objects, which this page treats only through routine bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: 'est en exp central' in the NB is likely 'est en effet central'.
In (21) the middle group is probably G*_{ρ,σ}(0) or G^0, written with a superscript; the marks are ambiguous.
'(dans M_{ρ,σ} + Antiinv)' is uncertain; it may read '(dans M_{ρ,σ} + Autom...)'.
The archive page number in the bottom-left corner is 400.
In (25) the arrow is an inclusion sign: μ2×μ2×μ2 ⊂ M^{0+}_{ρ,σ}.
